thread:
maria: billing-bot popped an alert for a large egress charge from logs backfill job just now. spike ~1.2TB ap-southeast-1 -> us-west-2, invoice preview shows ~USD100 on that transfer. not expected 🤔

billing-bot: [ALERT] Unexpected egress: 1.18 TB transferred between regions (ap-southeast-1 -> us-west-2). Estimated charge: $106.20. See billing console: https://billing.redwood.example/alerts/1872

maria: job id backfill-20240912-3 (telemetry namespace). It was a reshard retry from the nightly backfill. I think the syncer re-ran full shards instead of incremental ranges.

sam: can you paste the k8s job logs / command that kicked it off? was this a manual retry or cron?

maria: looks like cron triggered: `cron/backfill-nightly` requeued due to previous failure. logs show rsync command to s3 replica bucket. snippet: ```
$ kubectl logs job/backfill-20240912-3 -n telemetry
starting backfill shard_range=23..46
uploading /var/log/telemetry/shard-23-46 to s3://redwood-logs-usw/telemetry/2024-09-12
rsync --archive --progress /var/log/telemetry s3://redwood-logs-usw/telemetry --delete
```

joel: hmm rsync to the us-west mirror is expected for DR, but we shouldn't re-upload already-mirrored shards. were checksums skipped?

kira: we recently flipped `BACKFILL_STRICT_CHECKSUM=false` to speed retries for small shuffles. that would skip delta checks. could cause full reuploads. cc @maria

sam: ok that's the likely cause. rough math: 1.18 TB * $0.09/GB ≈ $106. (cloud provider egress rates vary, billing console gave that estimate). Not trillions, but still unexpected. We should consider short-term mitigation + longer term guardrails.

maria: I paused the cron and scaled the backfill job to 0: `kubectl scale job/backfill-20240912-3 --replicas=0 -n telemetry` and disabled the nightly trigger.

sam: please open a billing ticket with cloud and add the transfer IDs. Also add an internal incident so finance knows. I can scope whether this qualifies for invoice adjustment.

maria: opened BILL-4567: "ap-southeast -> us-west logs reupload from backfill job" with attachments (job logs, rsync commands, run id).

joel: action items: 1) revert BACKFILL_STRICT_CHECKSUM change or make it env-toggle per-run; 2) add pre-check in backfill that compares object etags before upload; 3) add egress budget alert for telemetry-sync > 200GB/day.

kira: will add feature toggle and a preflight checksum step. can we also shard transfers by region to avoid cross-region duplication when a shard is already in target?

sam: finance asks we also estimate committed egress / reserved data transfer credits? cloud has volume discount tiers; if telemetry syncs keep hitting cross-region volumes we should evaluate a monthly commitment. for now, set temporary quota.

maria: temporary quota set: telemetry-sync egress cap 500GB/day (enforced by syncer wrapper), and I've added an alert to PagerDuty if cap is hit.

deploy-bot: scheduled job backfill-nightly disabled by maria at 2024-09-12T02:45:12Z

sam: thanks. next steps: (A) engineering fixes (joel/kira) for checksum toggle and preflight; (B) short-term policy: egress cap + billing ticket (maria); (C) finance to evaluate commitment if monthly cross-region egress > 2TB (sam).

maria: I'll follow up in BILL-4567 with full cost breakdown and a proposal for either shifting mirror target or purchasing transfer credits.

joel: quick note — if we end up purchasing a commitment, let's consider routing telemetry mirrors via regional aggregator to reduce cross-region hops. could cut egress by ~40%.

kira: ok starting a PR to re-enable strict checksum by default and add a delta upload mode. ETA EOD tomorrow.

sam: great. closing slack thread after BILL-4567 has finance reply. :thumbsup:
